plants.name: Wisteria floribunda
plants.description: Long, fragrant flower clusters hang from twisting vines and form glowing tunnels and canopies. At Japan's famous wisteria gardens, the blooms open in a slow wave. Pale pink comes first, then deep purple, then white and yellow.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-April to mid-May, usually peaking from late April into early May. Some later varieties, including white ones, are still flowering around May 8.
plants.funFact: Wisteria vines twine in a set direction. Japanese wisteria climbs clockwise, while Chinese wisteria climbs counterclockwise. Old vines can grow into massive woody trunks that live for well over a century.

plants.name: Banksia serrata
plants.description: A rugged, gnarled coastal tree with big, upright, greenish-yellow flower spikes. Each spike is a dense bottlebrush of thousands of tiny flowers. Honeyeaters, bees and small mammals visit it for nectar. After flowering, the spikes turn into the woody seed cones that inspired the 'Banksia men' of Australian children's stories.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer through autumn in Australia. Early May falls in autumn, so the flower spikes are still opening.
plants.location: Coastal eastern Australia, from Queensland through New South Wales to Victoria and Tasmania
plants.funFact: Banksia seed cones are tough and fire-adapted. Many stay sealed on the tree for years and open to release their seeds only after a bushfire passes.
